# future.mizu: Parallel Future Backend using ‘mizu’

> **Note:** This package is an early prototype under development.

## Introduction

The **[future.mizu](https://future.mizu.futureverse.org)** package is a
backend for the **[future](https://future.futureverse.org)** framework,
also known as the [Futureverse](https://www.futureverse.org). The
Futureverse makes it easy to parallelize existing R code - often with
only a minor change of code. Most users interact with it via
higher-level packages such as
**[futurize](https://futurize.futureverse.org)**,
**[future.apply](https://future.apply.futureverse.org)**,
**[furrr](https://furrr.futureverse.org)**, and
**[doFuture](https://doFuture.futureverse.org)**, and you choose *where*
and *how* the code runs by setting a future backend with
[`plan()`](https://future.futureverse.org/reference/plan.html). This
package adds the `mizu_multisession` backend, which runs futures in
parallel on the local machine using the
**[mizu](https://cran.r-project.org/package=mizu)** package.

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`futurize`](https://futurize.futureverse.org)`)`\
[`plan`](https://future.futureverse.org/reference/plan.html)`(``future.mizu``::`[`mizu_multisession`](https://future.mizu.futureverse.org/reference/mizu_multisession.md)`)``  ``# parallelize on the current machine`\
\
`# A slow function`\
`slow_fcn`` ``<-`` ``function``(``x``)`` ``{`\
`  `[`Sys.sleep`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Sys.sleep.html)`(``1.0``)`\
`  ``x``^``2`\
`}`\
\
`# Example data`\
`xs`` ``<-`` ``1``:``10`\
\
`# Sequential and parallel base R apply`\
`ys`` ``<-`` `[`lapply`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/lapply.html)`(``xs``, ``slow_fcn``)`\
`ys`` ``<-`` `[`lapply`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/lapply.html)`(``xs``, ``slow_fcn``)`` ``|>`` `[`futurize`](https://futurize.futureverse.org/reference/futurize.html)`(``)`\
\
`# Sequential and parallel purrr map`\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`purrr`](https://purrr.tidyverse.org/)`)`\
`ys`` ``<-`` ``xs`` ``|>`` `[`map`](https://purrr.tidyverse.org/reference/map.html)`(``slow_fcn``)`\
`ys`` ``<-`` ``xs`` ``|>`` `[`map`](https://purrr.tidyverse.org/reference/map.html)`(``slow_fcn``)`` ``|>`` `[`futurize`](https://futurize.futureverse.org/reference/futurize.html)`(``)`\
\
`# Sequential and parallel foreach calls`\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`foreach`](https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/foreach)`)`\
`ys`` ``<-`` `[`foreach`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/foreach/man/foreach.html)`(``x ``=`` ``xs``)`` `[`%do%`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/foreach/man/foreach.html)` ``slow_fcn``(``x``)`\
`ys`` ``<-`` `[`foreach`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/foreach/man/foreach.html)`(``x ``=`` ``xs``)`` `[`%do%`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/foreach/man/foreach.html)` ``slow_fcn``(``x``)`` ``|>`` `[`futurize`](https://futurize.futureverse.org/reference/futurize.html)`(``)`

The only thing that differs from using [any other future
backend](https://www.futureverse.org/backends.html) is the
[`plan()`](https://future.futureverse.org/reference/plan.html) call. The
code does not have to change, it gives identical results, and it behaves
exactly the same.

## The mizu_multisession backend

| Backend | Description | Alternative in future package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `mizu_multisession` | parallel evaluation in separate R processes (on current machine) | `plan(multisession)` |

The **mizu** package runs parallel R workers on the local machine.
Instead of communicating via sockets, the main R process and the workers
exchange data via shared memory - POSIX shared memory on Linux and
macOS, and Win32 file mappings on Windows.

### Advantages

- Communication between the main R process and the workers is cheap,
  which means that work can be split up into many small futures without
  the overhead dominating.

- Large vectors and data frames are read by the workers in place,
  without each worker holding its own copy.

- It works on Linux, macOS, and Windows, and requires no additional
  setup.

### Limitations

- The workers always run on the local machine. For workers on other
  machines, or on a high-performance compute (HPC) cluster, use another
  future backend, e.g. `plan(cluster)` or
  **[future.batchtools](https://future.batchtools.futureverse.org)**.

- At most 64 workers are supported by **mizu**.

- Data is passed via shared memory, which is limited in size. For
  instance, Docker containers default to only 64 MB of shared memory,
  which might not be enough when passing large objects.

- Cancelling a future is advisory. A future that is already running on a
  worker cannot be interrupted; it runs to completion and its result is
  discarded.

- Using a single worker,
  `plan(future.mizu::mizu_multisession, workers = 1)`, falls back to
  sequential processing in the current R process, unless the number of
  workers is protected by [`I()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/AsIs.html),
  e.g. `workers = I(1)`.

## Installation

The package is not yet available on CRAN. To install the development
version, use:

\
[`install.packages`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/install.packages.html)`(``"future.mizu"``, repos ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"https://futureverse-devel.r-universe.dev"``, ``"https://cloud.r-project.org"``)``)`
